mainTopic: The מורדת: unresolved claims to her belongings, the twelve-month wait for a גט, the אגרת מרד for an ארוסה and a שומרת יבם, and the weekly amounts in the משנה (טרפעיקין and שבת)
overview: The גמרא first objects to a ruling made against רב זביד. That ruling decided a question that רבא never answered. Since the question has no answer, the rule is simple: if the מורדת already grabbed the item, she keeps it, and if she did not, the court does not give it to her. Next, a מורדת waits twelve months for her גט, and her husband does not feed her during that time. Then שמואל teaches that an אגרת מרד is written for an ארוסה but not for a שומרת יבם. A ברייתא seems to say the opposite. The גמרא tries several ways to settle this: who made the demand, then חליצה versus יבום. It finally says the ברייתא follows the earlier rule that יבום comes first, and שמואל follows the later rule that חליצה comes first. Last, the גמרא explains the coin טרפעיקין in the משנה as half a dinar. It begins to explain why שבת is counted when the wife's כתובה is reduced but not when the husband must add to it. That answer finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenging the ruling made against רב זביד
steps.stepSummary: The judge is asked how he could rule against רב זביד on a question that רבא never answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just because רב זביד is a great man, you turned the ruling against him? Didn't רב כהנא say that רבא asked this very question and never answered it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks a ruling made against רב זביד. The ruling decided a question that רבא had left unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד was too humble to protest, so the judge ruled against him. The challenge is that nobody may give a firm ruling on a question that רבא himself never resolved. Ruling against someone because he is too pious to object is not fair.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man; an important Torah scholar
You turned the judgment around
He raised it as an open question
And he did not resolve it

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב זְבִיד גַּבְרָא רַבָּה הוּא,
phrases.english: Because Rav Zevid is a great man,
you turned the judgment against him?
But didn't Rav Kahana say:

phrases.aramaic: מִיבַּעְיָא בָּעֵי לַהּ רָבָא, וְלָא פְּשִׁיט?!
phrases.english: Rava raised it as a question and did not resolve it?!
phrases.notes: The question was whether a rebellious wife keeps her worn-out clothes and belongings.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב זְבִיד גַּבְרָא רַבָּה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from before this section, where a ruling was made against רב זביד's family.
steps.kashyaTarget: The judge's ruling that the מורדת keeps the items
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא left the question unresolved, so no definite ruling can be given against either side.

steps.title: Unresolved question: whoever holds the item keeps it
steps.stepSummary: Since the question was never decided, the woman keeps what she grabbed, but the court does not hand her what she did not grab.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the question was never decided either way: if she grabbed the items, we do not take them from her. If she did not grab them, we do not give them to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical rule for this undecided question. The deciding factor is whether the woman already has the items in her hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a doubt cannot be settled, the court leaves things as they are. If she is already holding the items, we do not take them away. If she is not holding them, we do not take them from the husband to give to her.

keyTerms.meaning: She seized; she grabbed it on her own
We do not take it out of her hands
We do not give it to her

steps.whatToRemember: In an unresolved doubt about money, whoever already holds the item keeps it. If she grabbed it, it stays with her. If she did not, the court does not give it to her.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a ruling that the items belong to her. The court simply does not move things around when the law is unclear.

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא דְּלָא אִתְּמַר לָא הָכִי וְלָא הָכִי,
phrases.english: Now that it was not stated this way or that way,
if she seized it, we do not take it away from her;
if she did not seize it, we do not give it to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּלָא אִתְּמַר לָא הָכִי וְלָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical result of the challenge in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: If she grabbed it, she keeps it. If she did not, the court gives her nothing.

steps.title: A twelve-month wait for the גט, with no food support
steps.stepSummary: A מורדת waits twelve months before she gets her גט, and her husband does not feed her during that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: We make her wait twelve months for her גט. During those twelve months, she gets no food support from her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new rule about the מורדת. It is about how long she waits for her גט and whether she is supported while she waits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט is held back for a full year, which gives her time to change her mind. During that year the husband does not have to give her מזונות, because she is the one refusing him.

keyTerms.meaning: We delay; we make her wait
Twelve months of the year
The גט (bill of divorce)
Food support

phrases.aramaic: וּמְשַׁהֵינַן לַהּ תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא אַגִּיטָּא,
phrases.english: And we delay her twelve months of the year for the bill of divorce,
and during those twelve months of the year
she has no sustenance from the husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְשַׁהֵינַן לַהּ תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא אַגִּיטָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another practical rule about the מורדת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מורדת waits twelve months for her גט and receives no מזונות during that time.

steps.title: שמואל: an אגרת מרד is written for an ארוסה but not for a שומרת יבם
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the court writes a rebellion letter for an engaged woman, but not for a widow waiting for her יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טובי בר קיסנא said in the name of שמואל: the court writes an אגרת מרד for an ארוסה, but it does not write an אגרת מרד for a שומרת יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. שמואל tells us which women can be given a court letter declaring them rebellious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אגרת מרד is a court order that lets the court reduce her כתובה. שמואל says it applies even to an ארוסה, a woman who is only engaged. It does not apply to a שומרת יבם.

keyTerms.meaning: A letter of rebellion: a court order to reduce the כתובה of a rebellious wife
A betrothed woman: the first stage of marriage, before living together
A widow without children who is waiting for her late husband's brother (the יבם)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר קִיסְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Tuvi bar Kisna said that Shmuel said:
We write a letter of rebellion about a betrothed woman,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין כּוֹתְבִין אִגֶּרֶת מָרֶד עַל שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם.
phrases.english: but we do not write a letter of rebellion about a widow awaiting her yavam.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר קִיסְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: which women the אגרת מרד applies to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אגרת מרד is written for an ארוסה but not for a שומרת יבם.

steps.title: A ברייתא includes the שומרת יבם
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the rebellion rules apply equally to all these women, even a שומרת יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא challenges this: a ברייתא says it is all the same to me whether she is an ארוסה or a married woman. It applies even to a נדה, even to a sick woman, and even to a שומרת יבם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict שמואל. The ברייתא includes the שומרת יבם in the rebellion rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל left out the שומרת יבם, but the ברייתא lists her by name. So it looks like an אגרת מרד can be written for her too.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection from an earlier source
It is all the same to me
A fully married woman
A woman in her time of נדה

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
It is the same to me, a betrothed woman or a married woman,
even a menstruating woman, even an ill woman,
and even a widow awaiting her yavam!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's rule from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that no אגרת מרד is written for a שומרת יבם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly applies the rebellion rules to a שומרת יבם.

steps.title: It depends on who made the demand
steps.stepSummary: The two sources describe different cases: one where he asked for her and one where she asked for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not a problem. Here, he made the demand. There, she made the demand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by showing that each source is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is talking about the יבם asking to marry her while she refuses. In that case she is a real מורדת. שמואל is talking about her asking to marry the יבם while he refuses. In that case the court does not step in for her.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
He made the demand
She made the demand

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, where he made the demand,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא: the יבם wants to marry her and she refuses.

phrases.english: there, where she made the demand.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן שֶׁתָּבַע הוּא, כָּאן שֶׁתָּבְעָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source describes a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל and the ברייתא disagree about the שומרת יבם.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the יבם demands and she refuses, she is treated as a מורדת. When she demands and he refuses, the court does not act for her.

steps.title: Support from another teaching of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: שמואל himself says the court responds when he makes the demand, but not when she does.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב תחליפא בר אבימי said in the name of שמואל: if he made the demand, the court responds to him. If she made the demand, the court does not respond to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by quoting שמואל himself, who draws this exact line between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the split in step 6 is שמואל's own view and not just a forced answer. When he demands, the court treats her as a מורדת. When she demands, the court does not add to her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: The court responds to him and takes up his case
The court does not respond to her request

steps.whatToRemember: For a שומרת יבם, everything depends on who made the demand. If the יבם demands and she refuses, she can be made a מורדת. If she demands and he refuses, the court does not step in.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבִימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: As Rav Taḥalifa bar Avimi said that Shmuel said:
If he made the demand, we respond to him.
If she made the demand, we do not respond to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבִימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The split between 'he demanded' and 'she demanded'
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's teaching, as reported by רב תחליפא בר אבימי

steps.title: The wording of שמואל's ruling does not fit a case where she made the demand
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל was talking about a woman who made the demand, he should have said the letter is written 'for' her, not 'about' her.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did we explain שמואל? As a case where she made the demand. But then why does he say 'we write a rebellion letter about an engaged woman'? He should have said 'for an engaged woman'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the explanation from the earlier steps, that שמואל was talking about a woman who made the demand. It points out that his exact words don't fit that explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'about' (עַל) her sounds like the letter is written against her, as if she is the one rebelling. But in a case where she asked and he refused, he is the rebel. So the letter should be written 'for' her, on her behalf (לַאֲרוּסָה).

keyTerms.meaning: You set it up / explained it as a specific case
A rebellion letter that the court writes against the side that refuses
About / against
He should have said

phrases.english: In what case did you set up this statement of Shmuel?
Where she made the demand?
phrases.notes: This is the reading from earlier: she asked to marry, and he refused.

phrases.english: Then why this wording: 'We write a rebellion letter about an engaged woman'?
He should have said 'for an engaged woman'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the reading of שמואל set up in steps 6-7 against his exact words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that שמואל speaks about a case where the woman made the demand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'about' implies the letter is against her, which fits only if she is the rebel, not the one who asked.

steps.title: Fix the wording to say 'for an engaged woman'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this is not a real problem and simply reads שמואל's words as 'for' her.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. Read it as 'for an engaged woman.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the wording problem by correcting how we read שמואל's line. It keeps the explanation that she made the demand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the ruling itself changes, only one small word. The letter is written on her behalf, against the husband who refuses her.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult
Teach it / read it as
For (on behalf of) the engaged woman

phrases.english: This is not difficult;
Teach it as 'for an engaged woman.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's word 'about' seemed to make the woman the rebel.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it as 'for' her: the letter is written on her behalf against the man.

steps.title: Why no letter for a שומרת יבם?
steps.stepSummary: If she made the demand, why does the court help an engaged woman but not a שומרת יבם?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a שומרת יבם, that the court does not write a letter for her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind שמואל's split. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both women asked to be married and the man refused. So we need a reason why the court acts for one and not for the other.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to marry her or release her

phrases.english: What is different about a woman waiting for her yavam, that the court does not write a letter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the wording is fixed, asks for the reason behind the ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the court acts for an engaged woman but not for a שומרת יבם.

steps.title: She is told: you are not commanded
steps.stepSummary: The court tells the שומרת יבם to go away, since she has no command to have children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we say to her: Go away, you are not commanded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a reason: the court won't pressure the יבם for her, because she has no מצוה that requires it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her wish to be married is not backed by a command of her own. So the court has no grounds to force the man to act for her.

keyTerms.meaning: Go away
You are not commanded

phrases.english: Because we say to her:
Go away, you are not commanded.
phrases.notes: The court means she isn't commanded to have children, so it won't push him for her sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A woman is not commanded to have children, so the court does not act on her demand.

steps.title: The same reason should apply to an engaged woman
steps.stepSummary: An engaged woman is not commanded either, so why does the court help her?
steps.simpleTranslation: An engaged woman too: let us say to her, Go away, you are not commanded!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. The reason proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An engaged woman has no command to have children either. If that reason is enough to send away the שומרת יבם, it should send away the engaged woman too, yet שמואל says the court helps her.

keyTerms.meaning: An engaged woman (after קידושין, before the wedding)
Also / too
Let us say to her

phrases.english: An engaged woman too —
let us say to her: Go away, you are not commanded!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason applies just as much to the engaged woman, so it cannot explain why only the שומרת יבם is turned away.

steps.title: The engaged woman comes with a real claim
steps.stepSummary: The court helps the engaged woman because she has a real claim: she wants children to support and bury her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where she comes with a claim, saying: I want a staff for my hand and a hoe for my burial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the engaged woman in שמואל's ruling is not just asking. She brings a real reason the court accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even without a command, her personal need for children is a fair claim. So the court writes a letter on her behalf against the man who refuses.

keyTerms.meaning: She comes with a claim (a real reason)
A staff for the hand: children to lean on in old age
A hoe for burial: children to bury her

phrases.english: Rather, it is where she comes with a claim,
that she says:
I want a staff for my hand
and a hoe for my burial.
phrases.notes: She means children to lean on when she is old, and to bury her when she dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by narrowing the engaged woman's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The engaged woman is only asking, so 'you are not commanded' should apply to her too.
steps.terutzMaskana: She brings a real claim, the need for children, so the court acts for her.

steps.title: A שומרת יבם could bring the same claim
steps.stepSummary: A שומרת יבם can also come with a claim, so the difference still isn't explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too a שומרת יבם, where she comes with a claim?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again: the new answer gives the שומרת יבם the same right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a claim of needing children is enough, a שומרת יבם can say exactly the same thing. So the 'she made the demand' reading still can't explain why שמואל treats the two women differently.

keyTerms.meaning: So too / the same here
A claim or reason brought to court

phrases.english: So too a woman waiting for her yavam,
where she comes with a claim?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שומרת יבם can bring the identical claim, so the court should help her too, against שמואל.

steps.title: New reading: both cases are where he made the demand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the 'she made the demand' reading. In both sources he made the demand: the ברייתא is about חליצה, and שמואל is about יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both this and that are where he made the demand, and it is not difficult: here it is for חליצה, and there it is for יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on its earlier way of resolving the ברייתא against שמואל. It offers a brand-new split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the woman is the one refusing in both sources. If the יבם asked her to do חליצה and she refused, the ברייתא says a letter is written against her. If he asked to do יבום and she refused, שמואל says no letter is written.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that
Where he made the demand
To do חליצה, the ceremony that releases her
To do יבום, marrying his brother's widow

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. Here the man asks and the woman refuses, the opposite of the reading in steps 8-14, where she asked.

phrases.english: Rather, both this and that are where he made the demand,
and it is not difficult:
here it is to do chalitzah, and there it is to do yibum.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא, where a letter is written, is about חליצה; שמואל, where no letter is written, is about יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Abandons the resolution of step 6 after step 14 undermined it, and offers a new split.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different split between the cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sources split by who made the demand, him or her.
steps.terutzMaskana: He made the demand in both: for חליצה the court acts against her, for יבום it does not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן supports the חליצה/יבום split
steps.stepSummary: רבי פדת quotes רבי יוחנן: if he demands חליצה the court responds, but if he demands יבום it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי פדת said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If he demanded to do חליצה, the court responds to him. If he demanded to do יבום, the court does not respond to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its new split with a clear ruling from an אמורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's ruling matches the new reading exactly. The court backs the יבם who wants חליצה, but not the יבם who wants יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who passes on רבי יוחנן's teachings
The court responds to him and acts on his request
The court does not respond to him

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling becomes the basis for the new reading. The next steps ask for the reason behind it.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי פְּדָת אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Pedat said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
If he demanded to do chalitzah, the court responds to him.
If he demanded to do yibum, the court does not respond to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי פְּדָת אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the new split of step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The split between a demand for חליצה and a demand for יבום
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי פדת in the name of רבי יוחנן

steps.title: Why doesn't the court back a demand for יבום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the court won't act when the יבם wants יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about יבום, that the court does not respond?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind רבי יוחנן's ruling. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both requests are part of the יבום laws. So we need a reason why her refusal counts as rebellion in one case and not in the other.

keyTerms.meaning: That it does not (the court does not act)
Marrying the widow of a brother who died without children

phrases.english: What is different about yibum, that the court does not respond?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling quoted in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the court won't treat her refusal of יבום as rebellion.

steps.title: He is told to marry someone else
steps.stepSummary: The court tells the יבם to go marry another woman, so her refusal is not rebellion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we say to him: Go and marry another woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the יבם has no need to marry this specific woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He can have a family with any other wife. So the court does not force her into a marriage she refuses.

keyTerms.meaning: And marry
Another woman

phrases.english: Because we say to him:
Go and marry another woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמְרִינַן לֵיהּ: זִיל וּנְסֵיב אִיתְּתָא אַחֲרִיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He can marry a different woman, so her refusal of יבום is not treated as rebellion.

steps.title: The same reason should apply to חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The יבם who wants חליצה could also be told to marry someone else, so the split is still unexplained.
steps.simpleTranslation: With חליצה too, let us say to him: Go and marry another woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The same reasoning seems to cover the חליצה case. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he can simply marry someone else, he doesn't need her חליצה either. So why should the court act against her when she refuses חליצה? The difference between the two cases is still unclear.

keyTerms.meaning: With חליצה too

phrases.english: With chalitzah too,

phrases.aramaic: נֵימָא לֵיהּ: זִיל וּנְסֵיב אִיתְּתָא אַחֲרִיתִי!
phrases.english: let us say to him: Go and marry another woman!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason applies equally to a demand for חליצה, so it cannot explain why the court acts only in that case.

steps.title: The יבם who wants חליצה cannot find another wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 19. The court backs a יבם who wants חליצה because, as long as she is tied to him, no one will give him another wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason is that he says: 'Since she is tied to me, they will not give me another wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 19. It gives a real reason why the court helps a יבם who wants חליצה: while she is tied to him, he cannot get married to anyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18, the reason the court does not back a יבם who wants יבום was 'go marry someone else.' Step 19 asked: why can't we tell the יבם who wants חליצה the same thing? Here is the answer: he cannot marry someone else. Families will not give him a wife while a יבמה who might still do יבום with him is tied to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Tied, bound (she is still bound to the יבם through the bond of זיקה)
Another woman, another wife
They will not give me (a wife in marriage)

phrases.english: Rather, it is because he says:
'Since she is tied to me,'
'they will not give me another wife.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19 by showing that 'go marry someone else' does not work for the יבם who wants חליצה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason that separates the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יבם who wants חליצה could also be told to go marry another woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: He cannot. While she is tied to him, no one will give him a wife, so his demand for חליצה is valid and her refusal counts as rebellion.

steps.title: The same claim works for the יבם who wants יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. A יבם who wants יבום can make the exact same claim: 'since she is tied to me, no one will give me another wife.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too he can say: 'Since she is tied to me, they will not give me another wife!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer it just gave. The same problem exists when the יבם asks for יבום and she refuses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases she is still tied to him and stops him from marrying anyone else. So the reason from step 20 does not explain why רבי יוחנן's rule (step 16) treats the two demands differently. The split between חליצה and יבום falls apart again.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, the same applies in this case

phrases.english: Here too:
phrases.notes: "Here" means the case where the יבם asked for יבום and she refused.

phrases.english: 'Since she is tied to me,'
'they will not give me another wife!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the reason given in step 20 applies to both cases, so it cannot tell them apart.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between demanding חליצה and demanding יבום (steps 16–20)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being stuck without another wife is a problem whether he wants חליצה or יבום. A reason found in both cases cannot explain why the law treats them differently.

steps.title: Both sources deal with יבום, from different periods
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. Both the ברייתא and שמואל speak of a יבם who wants יבום. The ברייתא follows the earlier משנה, and שמואל follows the later משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both cases are where he asked to do יבום, and there is no contradiction. Here, the ruling follows the earlier משנה. There, it follows the later משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the חליצה-versus-יבום split and gives a brand-new answer. The two sources disagree because each one follows a different stage of the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is the same in both sources: the יבם wants יבום and she refuses. The ברייתא, which writes a letter of rebellion, follows the early rule, when יבום was the preferred מצוה. שמואל, who does not write one, follows the later rule, when חליצה was preferred. Under the later rule, refusing יבום is not rebellion.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, both sources
He demanded to do יבום
The earlier version of a משנה (an older ruling)
The later version of a משנה (the ruling that replaced it)

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not build on the reasons in steps 18–20. It sets the חליצה-versus-יבום split aside and explains the conflict by time period instead.

phrases.english: Rather, this one and that one
are where he demanded to do יבום,
and it is not difficult:
here, it follows the earlier משנה,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the ברייתא, which does write a letter of rebellion.

phrases.english: there, it follows the later משנה.
phrases.notes: "There" is שמואל, who says the court does not write one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי שֶׁתָּבַע לְיַיבֵּם, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed חליצה-versus-יבום split with a split between earlier and later rulings.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different time periods (משנה ראשונה versus משנה אחרונה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources had to be about different demands (חליצה versus יבום) to avoid a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are about a demand for יבום. They differ only because each follows a different stage of the law about which מצוה comes first.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the final answer to the contradiction between the ברייתא and שמואל, and it ties the letter-of-rebellion rule to the change in preference from יבום to חליצה.

steps.title: The משנה that shows the change from יבום first to חליצה first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה showing that at first יבום came before חליצה, but later, when people no longer did it for the sake of the מצוה, חליצה was put first.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: The מצוה of יבום comes before the מצוה of חליצה. That was in earlier times, when people meant to do it for the sake of the מצוה. Now that people do not mean to do it for the sake of the מצוה, the חכמים said: the מצוה of חליצה comes before the מצוה of יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the 'earlier' and 'later' rulings it just mentioned. It shows that the law really did change over time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the earlier rule, יבום was the main מצוה, so a woman who refused it was rebelling. That fits the ברייתא. Under the later rule, יבום was no longer done with pure intentions, so חליצה became preferred. Refusing יבום then is not rebellion, which fits שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes first, takes priority
They had in mind to do it for the sake of the מצוה
In earlier times, originally
Now, in later times

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא (letter of rebellion against a יבמה who refuses יבום) follows the old rule that יבום comes first. שמואל (no letter) follows the later rule that חליצה comes first.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
The מצוה of יבום comes before the מצוה of חליצה —
that was in earlier times,
when they would have in mind the sake of the מצוה.
Now that they do not have in mind the sake of the מצוה,
they said: the מצוה of חליצה
comes before the מצוה of יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the earlier and later rulings named in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that there was an earlier ruling (יבום first) and a later ruling (חליצה first)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in בכורות 13a: מִצְוַת יִבּוּם קוֹדֶמֶת לְמִצְוַת חֲלִיצָה, and later, מִצְוַת חֲלִיצָה קוֹדֶמֶת

steps.title: What is a טרפעיק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about reducing a rebellious wife's כתובה and asks what the coin רבי יהודה calls טרפעיקין is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Until when does he reduce...' What are טרפעיקין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה's words and asks what the coin טרפעיקין means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה measures the weekly amount in טרפעיקין, not in דינרין. To know how much money is involved, we first need to know what this coin is.

keyTerms.meaning: Reduces (takes money off the כתובה)
A type of coin mentioned by רבי יהודה in the משנה
What is

phrases.english: 'Until when does he reduce,' etc.
phrases.notes: These are words quoted from our משנה about taking money off the כתובה of a wife who rebels; וכו׳ means the quote goes on.

phrases.english: What are טרפעיקין?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the letter-of-rebellion discussion and returns to explain a word in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning and value of the coin טרפעיקין in רבי יהודה's opinion

steps.title: A טרפעיק is an אסתירא, worth half a dinar
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says a טרפעיק is an אסתירא, and an אסתירא is worth half a זוז (dinar).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: An אסתירא. And how much is an אסתירא? Half a זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question with another coin's name, and then the גמרא gives that coin's value: half a dinar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming the coin is not enough, so the גמרא adds a short follow-up question to pin down its value. With this, we know רבי יהודה's amounts are half the size they would be in דינרין.

keyTerms.meaning: A small coin
Half
A זוז, the same as a dinar

phrases.english: רב ששת said: An אסתירא.
And how much is an אסתירא?
Half a זוז.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A טרפעיק is an אסתירא, which is worth half a dinar.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms the half-dinar value
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה says three טרפעיקין equal nine מעין, a מעה and a half for each day. This matches the half-dinar value.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. רבי יהודה says: Three טרפעיקין, which are nine מעין, a מעה and a half for each day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב ששת. The numbers in it only work if a טרפעיק is half a dinar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dinar is six מעין, so half a dinar is three מעין. Three טרפעיקין are then nine מעין, just as the ברייתא says. Spread over six days, that comes to a מעה and a half per day.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this (support for the statement just made)
A small coin, one sixth of a dinar (plural מֵעִין)

steps.whatToRemember: A טרפעיק is an אסתירא, worth half a dinar (three מעין). That is why רבי יהודה's three טרפעיקין equal nine מעין.

phrases.english: A ברייתא also teaches this,
רבי יהודה says: Three טרפעיקין,
which are nine מעין,
phrases.notes: A dinar is six מעין, so each half-dinar טרפעיק is three מעין.

phrases.english: a מעה and a half for each day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב ששת's answer from step 25 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's claim that a טרפעיק is worth half a dinar
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה: three טרפעיקין are nine מעין, a מעה and a half per day

steps.title: Why does the husband get credit for שבת but the wife does not?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף asks שמואל why שבת is counted when the wife's כתובה is reduced, but not counted when the husband must add to her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף said to שמואל: Why is it different for him, that we give him the money for שבת? And why is it different for her, that we do not give her the money for שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question comes up about the numbers in the משנה. When the wife rebels, the husband gains for all seven days, including שבת. When the husband rebels, the wife gains for only six days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seven דינרים a week for the wife means one דינר a day, so שבת is included. The ברייתא in the last step showed the husband adds a מעה and a half a day for six days, so שבת is left out. רבי חייא בר יוסף wants to know why the two sides are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why are these two cases treated differently?
He (here, the husband)
She (here, the wife)
We give
The amount for שבת

steps.confusionAlert: "We give him" does not mean the husband is handed cash. It means the wife's כתובה goes down, so he gains. In the same way, "we give her" means the husband must add to her כתובה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף לִשְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef said to Shmuel:
What is different about him (when she rebels),
that we give him the amount for Shabbat?
And what is different about her (when he rebels),
that we do not give her the amount for Shabbat?
phrases.notes: The ברייתא in step 26 counted only six days for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא אִיהוּ דְּיָהֲבִינַן לֵיהּ דְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the six-day count shown in step 26 and compares it with the seven-day count for the wife.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason שבת is counted when the wife is fined but not when the husband is fined.

steps.title: Taking money off does not look like being paid for שבת
steps.stepSummary: The answer explains that lowering her כתובה does not look like שבת wages, but adding to it would. The answer finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it is she whose כתובה is being reduced, it does not look like being paid for שבת. But when it is he who must keep adding to her כתובה...
steps.whatsHappening: The answer begins. It explains the wife's side here and starts explaining the husband's side, which finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being paid for שבת (שכר שבת) is not allowed. When money is taken off the wife's כתובה, nobody is being paid, so counting שבת is fine. When the husband must add money for each day, adding for שבת would look like paying her for שבת, so that day is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is being reduced, going down
It does not look like
Wages for שבת, payment earned for שבת, which is not allowed
He is adding on

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that חז"ל avoided even the look of being paid for שבת, even in a fine set by בית דין.

phrases.english: She, whose amount is being reduced,
it does not look like Shabbat wages;
he, who is adding on,
phrases.notes: The sentence finishes on the next amud: adding for שבת would look like שבת wages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lowering her כתובה does not look like שכר שבת, so שבת is counted. Adding to it would look like שכר שבת, so שבת is left out. The second half finishes on the next amud.
